# Five-minute pitch — teleprompter script

**Read the bold text aloud. Brackets are stage directions, not spoken.**

Every figure is rendered from `results/metrics.json`. Before recording:

```bash
python scripts/collect_metrics.py && python scripts/render_docs.py && python scripts/ci_gates.py all
```

**How to say the numbers.** Precise figures live in the on-screen directions so
the viewer reads them while you speak plainly. Where one is spoken, read it to
two decimals — "zero point two nine" — never digit by digit.

**The headline figure is spoken aloud at 2:05, so it is checked.**
`tests/test_pitch_script.py` asserts the words in that line still match the
measured precision at ten. If the measurement moves, the test fails and names
the line to fix, rather than letting you read a stale number to camera.

**The one thing the renderer cannot check** is the plain-English gloss beside
each figure ("call it three in ten"). If a number moves a lot, fix its gloss by
hand.

**Budget:** about 660 spoken words — roughly four and a half minutes at a
comfortable pace. The three pauses take it to five. Do not rush them.

---

## [0:00 – 0:30] The problem

*[ON SCREEN: the queue, cases listed.]*

> **Every risk team already has fraud detectors. None of them has enough
> analysts.**
>
> **The bottleneck isn't detection. It's investigation. An analyst gets an alert
> on one transaction, then spends an hour finding who else was involved.**
>
> **Mule fraud isn't one account. It's a ring. An alert shows you one node of
> it. Sentinel changes the unit — it flags the whole ring, already
> investigated.**

*[ON SCREEN: `scripts/eval_cost.py` output. Break-even

> ours, and it isn't flattering.**
>

> rupee figure. We invert it and report break-even precision — the number you
> can check even if you reject every assumption we made.**
>

> the list. Push them by ten times, and break-even goes above one. That's a
> precision no detector can reach, including a perfect one.**
>
> **At that point our own queue doesn't pay for itself. We'd rather tell you
> than have you find it.**

## Before you hit record

- **Re-render and check the gates are green.** One command, top of this page.
- **Practice the three pauses** — 1:25, 2:05, and 4:20. They carry the pitch.
- **Don't say "nobody has this."** Razorpay built Vulcan. The RBI runs
  MuleHunter across twenty-three banks. Graph AML tooling is a mature market.
  The rare thing is honest ring-level measurement, not the idea.
- **Don't promise a perfect queue.** It contradicts everything else you say.
- **Don't ask for compute.** A full replay runs in under a minute and a three
  times speedup already shipped. Ask for data.
- **Don't name the other entrants.** The "who made the test data" line makes the
  point without naming anyone, which is stronger.
- **Lead with one domain.** The synthetic-identity work is honest and built, but
  it splits attention. Mention it only if asked.
- **Don't inflate the defect count.** Seventeen are numbered in the code; the
  catalogue carries more because later ones were recorded in commit messages
  rather than renumbered. `docs/WHAT-BROKE.md` says it plainly: "the count is
  not the point, the catch mechanism is." An unsourced round number spoken on
  camera is the exact failure this project is built to prevent.
